name: P01 rawTexEndPops: the top starts one place low
why: the first name is read against the place under the real top; run alone, killed by non-clock rows of `raw-tex-end-equivalence.test.ts` (a closer on the line under its opener) and by every enumeration of `raw-tex-end-pops-equivalence.test.ts`

name: P02 rawTexEndPops: the top starts one place high
why: the first name is read against a place past the end, which is `undefined`, so nothing ever pops; run alone, killed by the same two files as P01

name: P03 rawTexEndPops: the stack is read at a top of zero
why: EQUIVALENT: `top >= 0` differs from `top > 0` only at `top === 0`, where the read is `stack[-1]`, which is `undefined`, and a name is always a string, so the comparison refuses either way

name: P04 rawTexEndPops: the bottom environment is never popped
why: the bottom environment (`top === 1`) can never be popped, so `\begin{a}` ... `\end{a}` with nothing else open stays open; run alone, killed by `raw-tex-end-equivalence.test.ts` (a one-environment document) and by the enumerations

name: P05 rawTexEndPops: the place above the top is read
why: the name is compared with the place ABOVE the top, which is `undefined` for the first name; run alone, killed by non-clock rows of `raw-tex-end-equivalence.test.ts` and by the enumerations

name: P06 rawTexEndPops: the place two below the top is read
why: the name is compared with the place two below the top; run alone, killed by non-clock rows of `raw-tex-end-equivalence.test.ts` and by the enumerations

name: P07 rawTexEndPops: a name that is NOT the top pops it
why: a name that is not the top pops it (and the top pops nothing); run alone, killed by non-clock rows of `raw-tex-end-equivalence.test.ts` (an unterminated opener after a closer) and by the enumerations

name: P08 rawTexEndPops: loose equality
why: EQUIVALENT: both sides are strings, or `undefined` against a string, and `==` refuses that pair exactly as `===` does (a stack entry and a name are never `null`)

name: P09 rawTexEndPops: a pop lowers the top by two
why: a pop lowers the top by two, so the environment under the popped one is skipped; run alone, killed by the review rows of `raw-tex-end-equivalence.test.ts` (the stack that is left after a line) and by the enumerations

name: P10 rawTexEndPops: a pop empties the stack
why: a pop empties the stack, so `\end{b}\end{a}` over `[a, b]` counts one and a later `\end{a}` finds nothing open; run alone, killed by the same review rows and the enumerations

name: P11 rawTexEndPops: a pop raises the top
why: a pop RAISES the top (the next read is past the end); run alone, killed by the same review rows and the enumerations

name: P12 rawTexEndPops: the count starts at one
why: the count starts at one, so a line that closes nothing counts as closing one; run alone, killed by non-clock rows of `raw-tex-end-equivalence.test.ts` (`\end{b\end{a}` names `b\end{a`, so `a` is never closed) and by the enumerations

name: P13 rawTexEndPops: the answer is what is left open
why: the answer is what is left open, not what was closed; run alone, killed by non-clock rows of `raw-tex-end-equivalence.test.ts` and by the enumerations

name: P14 rawTexEndPops: the answer is the drop in depth
why: EQUIVALENT: `top` starts at `stack.length` and falls by exactly one for each pop, so `stack.length - top` is `pops` on every input

name: P15 rawTexEndPops: the count is capped at 4096
why: the count is capped at 4,096; the two exhaustive enumerations pop at most six from a line, the seeded sample twelve, and the documents of the older rows fewer, so only the 5,000-closer rows of `raw-tex-end-pops-equivalence.test.ts` tell it apart (run alone, they are the only kill)

name: P16 rawTexEndPops: the count is capped at 16
why: the count is capped at 16; run alone, killed only by the 5,000-closer rows of `raw-tex-end-pops-equivalence.test.ts`

name: P17 rawTexEndPops: the stack is copied once per call (answers kept, cost the depth per call)
why: the stack is copied once per call: every answer is kept, the cost is the depth per call; run alone, killed by the clock row 'a closer that is the top' of the deep-stack rows of `raw-tex-end-pops-equivalence.test.ts` (30,000 calls over 100,000 places) and by the document clock rows of `s340-raw-tex-stack-rows.test.ts` (80,000 closing lines over an 80,000-deep stack; the review round of Session 340 timed 2,730 and 4,888 ms against the limit of 1,000 and the controls unmoved), and by nothing that reads an answer

name: P18 rawTexEndPops: the open part of the stack is sliced for every name (answers kept, cost the depth per name)
why: the open part of the stack is sliced for every name: every answer is kept, the cost is the depth per name; run alone, killed by the clock row 'a closer that is the top' of the deep-stack rows and by clock rows of `s340-raw-tex-stack-rows.test.ts` (97 s to kill: the document rows run to their end)

from:

name: P22 probe call: only the first 1,000 characters of the line are read
from: const texEndPops: number = texEnv !== null && texEnv[1] === "end" ? rawTexEndPops(rawTexEnvStack, line) : 0;
to: const texEndPops: number = texEnv !== null && texEnv[1] === "end" ? rawTexEndPops(rawTexEnvStack, line.slice(0, 1000)) : 0;

name: P23 probe call: the count of a line that is not a closer is one
from: const texEndPops: number = texEnv !== null && texEnv[1] === "end" ? rawTexEndPops(rawTexEnvStack, line) : 0;
to: const texEndPops: number = texEnv !== null && texEnv[1] === "end" ? rawTexEndPops(rawTexEnvStack, line) : 1;

name: P24 rawTexEndPops: only the first 65,536 places of the stack are read
why: only the first 65,536 places of the stack are read, so a stack deeper than that answers with the wrong top; run alone, killed by the deep-stack rows of `raw-tex-end-pops-equivalence.test.ts` (their top is a name no other place holds)
